$comment: caliper.toml: The eval config, TOML, passed to `caliper eval --config` (any file name). Relative paths (`golden`, `decide`, `fake_script`) resolve against the config file's folder.

max_regression.title: Max Regression
max_regression.description: allowed cost-weighted regression per row beyond replay noise

require.description: which CI bound the gate reads

max_error_rate.title: Max Error Rate
max_error_rate.description: Share of results allowed to end with no decision; --max-error-rate overrides it.

max_cost_ratio.title: Max Cost Ratio
max_cost_ratio.description: Fail a candidate whose mean cost per execution is above this multiple of the reference's (1.0 = "no more expensive"). A candidate or reference with replies priced at $0 fails too: an unknown price must not read as free.

quality_per_cost.title: Quality Per Cost
quality_per_cost.description: A candidate that costs more than the reference must be better by at least this many times its extra cost, judged by human approvals (needs [quality]): 1.0 means 10% more cost needs at least 10% fewer errors than the reference.

quality_confidence.title: Quality Confidence
quality_confidence.description: How sure the quality rule must be: the confidence of the intervals it reads. 0.95 puts the burden of proof on the costlier candidate; 0.8 is more lenient; 0 compares point estimates.

quality_cost_tolerance.title: Quality Cost Tolerance
quality_cost_tolerance.description: Cost ratios up to 1 + this are treated as token-count noise, not extra cost.

thresholds.title: Thresholds
thresholds.description: score thresholds to report precision/coverage at

target_precision.title: Target Precision
target_precision.description: Recommend the lowest threshold reaching this precision; --target-precision overrides it.

Candidate.description: What is being evaluated. The identity is the whole tuple, not the model.

provider.description: fake is offline and free; the others call (and bill) a provider

model.title: Model
model.description: the provider's model id, e.g. a Bedrock inference profile id

thinking_budget_tokens.title: Thinking Budget Tokens
thinking_budget_tokens.description: thinking budget, where the provider takes one

output_mode.description: text, provider-native JSON schema, or a tool call

output_schema.title: Output Schema
output_schema.description: JSON Schema for json_schema / tool output

params.title: Params
params.description: Extra request params (temperature etc.); openai_compat reads its key from the env var named by params.api_key_env (default OPENAI_API_KEY).

base_url.title: Base Url
base_url.description: openai_compat endpoint, or an Anthropic API base URL

Candidate.title: Candidate

CostProjectionConfig.description:
Production volume, to turn cost per row into dollars per month (``[cost_projection]``).

``calls_per_day`` counts feature calls, i.e. golden-row equivalents (a vote
loop's 3 replies are one call).
CostProjectionConfig.title: CostProjectionConfig

GateRequirement.description:
What the regression gate must be able to say about a candidate.

Both read the paired bootstrap CI of ``excess = regression - replay noise``
(see ``caliper_eval.transitions.compute_paired_excess``):

* ``non_inferiority`` (default): pass only when the CI's **upper** bound is
  within ``max_regression``. A pass means "no worse than the reference
  beyond replay noise + max_regression, at 95%".
* ``no_evidence_of_regression``: fail only when the CI's **lower** bound is
  above ``max_regression``. A pass then only means "no detectable
  regression"; small golden sets pass easily. Use knowingly.
GateRequirement.title: GateRequirement

LabelSource.description: Who produced a label. Agreement with LLM_TEACHER is 'teacher agreement', never accuracy.
LabelSource.title: LabelSource

OperatingPointConfig.description:
Matched-operating-point comparison (``[operating_point]``).

``auto_outcomes`` are the outcomes that count as "handled automatically"
(auto-published, expensive call skipped, ...). The reference's share of
those on val is the coverage the candidate's score threshold is matched to.
OperatingPointConfig.title: OperatingPointConfig

output.title: Output
output.description: USD per million output tokens (reasoning tokens bill as output)

QualityConfig.description:
Human approvals of outcomes, to measure "better" (``[quality]``).

See :mod:`caliper_eval.approvals` for the file format and what counts.

approvals.title: Approvals
approvals.description: Approval JSONL files, relative to the config file (`caliper review` builds them).

golden_labels.title: Golden Labels
golden_labels.description: Also count human golden labels: the labelled outcome is approved, any other rejected.

base_sample.title: Base Sample
base_sample.description: Rows drawn uniformly at random (config seed) to measure the reference's error rate, which "X% fewer errors" needs; `caliper review` lists the same rows.

QualityConfig.title: QualityConfig

SliceConfig.description:
A named hard slice with its own pass rule (``[[slices]]``).

A row belongs to the slice when ``name`` is in ``GoldenRow.slices`` or when
it matches ``where`` (``{"stratum": "x"}`` / ``{"metadata.key": value}``;
a list value means "any of"). ``label_sources`` restricts which label
sources a label-based rule reads (default: ``min_precision`` reads human
sources only, ``must_not_lose`` reads every labelled row).

name.title: Name
name.description: also matches rows whose `slices` list holds this name

label_sources.title: Label Sources
label_sources.description: label sources a label-based rule reads

SliceConfig.title: SliceConfig

golden.title: Golden
golden.description: golden JSONL, relative to the config file

decide.title: Decide
decide.description: "file.py:func" turning a row's replies into a Decision

noise_replays.title: Noise Replays
noise_replays.description: times the reference is replayed (noise floor)

budget_usd.title: Budget Usd
budget_usd.description: stop before spending more than this

candidates.title: Candidates
candidates.description: [[candidates]]; the first one is the reference unless `reference` says otherwise.
